promptLatex: Which proof strategy is most appropriate for proving 'there is no largest prime number'?
hintLatex: Proof by contradiction is the natural strategy for existential negation claims.
Assume there is a largest prime, then construct a new prime larger than it.
This leads to the classic Euclid argument.
solutionLatex: Proof by contradiction: Assume there is a largest prime p. Consider the number N = (product of all primes up to p) + 1. N has a prime factor not in the original list, contradicting the assumption that p was the largest prime. Therefore no largest prime exists.
